facts.text: Sunshine earned its name when the original Braybrook Junction was officially renamed in July 1907, turning a tiny settlement into an industrial township.
The Sunshine Harvester Works, once the largest manufacturing plant in Australia, pioneered mass production of agricultural machinery and sparked the landmark Harvester Judgement labor case.
During World War II the same factory switched to munitions, producing shell casings, radar equipment and armored vehicle parts for Australian forces.
Sunshine’s early growth was fueled by rail access, which let the harvester factory export machinery across Australia and beyond.
The suburb’s multicultural character today reflects waves of migration that followed its industrial boom, bringing people from Europe, Asia and Africa.
Sunshine hosts the Victoria Scottish Pipes & Drums, one of Australia’s oldest continuously functioning pipe bands, founded by the factory’s employees.
